## Your task
Take the C slice file `output/layer0/foo/foo.c` (a stub slice) and generate ACSL annotations so that Frama-C WP can prove the original assert `//@ assert(y != 0);` inside the branch `if (x == 20) {}`. Produce an annotated file and verify it.

## Input file
`output/layer0/foo/foo.c` — content:
```
void foo(int x, int y);
extern int unknown();

void foo(int x, int y) {
  // loop body
  while (unknown()) {
    x  = x + 10;
    y  = y + 10;
  }
  // post-condition
  if (x == 20) {
    //@ assert(y != 0);
  }
}
```
The original contract (already part of the original source) is:
```
/*@
  requires 0 <= x <= 10;
  requires 0 <= y <= 10;
*/
```
This requires must be preserved.

## Semantics to annotate (understand this, then encode as ACSL)
The loop runs some unknown number of times (unknown() returns arbitrary nonzero). Each iteration adds 10 to BOTH x and y. At function entry x,y in [0,10]. After the loop, if x == 20, then the loop must have executed at least twice (since x<=10 at entry and each iteration adds 10, x in [0,10] can reach 20 only after at least one iteration), so y >= 10 > 0, so y != 0. A clean loop invariant that makes this provable is:
- `y - x == <initial value of (y - x)>` i.e. use `\at(y - x, Pre) - \at(x, Pre)` pattern, OR the simpler invariant `y >= x - 10` (which is established at loop entry because y>=0 and x-10<=0, and preserved because both x and y increase by 10). With `y >= x - 10` and `x == 20` you get `y >= 10 > 0`.

You may also add the invariant `10 <= x <= 20` style bounds if helpful, and the range `0 <= x` etc. Use whatever invariant set lets WP prove the assert cleanly. Add a proper loop annotation: `loop invariant`, `loop assigns x, y;`, and `loop variant` if feasible (loop variant may not be provable since unknown() is arbitrary — it is acceptable that the termination/loop variant is left out or not proved; the critical goal is proving the assert).

## Add the function contract
The function already has `/*@ requires 0 <= x <= 10; requires 0 <= y <= 10; */`. Add `assigns \nothing;` (the function does not modify caller state; x,y are by-value parameters). A postcondition is optional.

## Hard constraints
- NEVER use `admit`, `assume`, `axiom`, or `external_body`.
- Do NOT modify any original C token. Only ADD ACSL annotations (comments). The original `//@ assert(y != 0);` must remain EXACTLY in place, unchanged.
- Preserve the `requires` contract lines unchanged.
